```{r setup}
#| include: false
source("theme.R")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 5, fig.height = 3)
library(housepi)
set.seed(42)
```

In housepi we follow the convention for infectivity profiles to be function of the generation time.
Generation time is defined as the time from infection to transmission.

Certain profiles will then be conditioned on individuals incubation periods

<div style="display: flex; justify-content: center;">
<div>

| Delay                 | Infector | Infectee | Supported |
|-----------------------|:--------:|:--------:|:---------:|
| Generation Time       | &cross;  | &cross;  |  &check;  |
| Onset to Transmission | &check;  | &cross;  |  &check;  |
| Serial Time           | &check;  | &check;  |  &cross;  |

</div>
</div>

In addition, infectivity profiles in housepi can be of two kinds:

* **generic**: if all individuals share the same profile;
* **augmented**: if profile depends on individual covariates.

At any time one can provide a custom choice for the infectivity profile, however all models depending on profiles have a templated definition incorporated.  

To inspect definitions of templated profile definitions, we can proceed as follows.
We consider the model "augmented infection time" introduced in [Get started](housepi.html).
The model template comes in continuous time and with a templated infectivity profile which is chosen to be a gamma distribution parametrized with `mean = 2` and `var = 1`.
This can be accessed by calling `get_infec_profile`

```{r}
hhcontinuos <- new_housepi_model("augmented infection time")
# extract current loaded profile definitions
defs <- get_infec_profile(hhcontinuos)
defs
```

```{r}
profile <- expose_infec_profile(defs$func, defs$func_args)
infec <- dplyr::tibble(gentime = seq(0, 10, 0.01),
                       inst = profile$pdf(gentime),
                       cumul = profile$cdf(gentime))
```

```{r}
#| fig.alt: >
#|  Instantaneous infectivity profile as a function of the generation time in black.
#|  On a second axis in orange, the corresponding cumulative infectivity profile.

# plot instantaneous and cumulative profile with ggplot2
library(ggplot2)

# coefficient to rescale cumulative
rescale <- max(infec$cumul) / max(infec$inst)

ggplot(infec, aes(x = gentime)) +
  # plot cumulative profile
  theme(axis.ticks.y.right = element_line(color = "coral"),
        axis.text.y.right = element_text(color = "coral"),
        axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = "coral")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = cumul / rescale), color = "coral") +
  # plot instantaneous
  geom_line(aes(y = inst), color = "black") +
  # apply rescaling
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Instantaneous",
                     sec.axis = sec_axis(~. * rescale, name = "Cumulative")) +
  labs(x = "Generation Time")
```

## Case of Discrete Models

To move to discrete time we need to specify it at the moment of the model generation by adding the option `discr = TRUE`.
This model requires compilation as for all custom models.

```{r}
hhdiscrete <- new_housepi_model("augmented infection time", discr = TRUE, 
                                quiet = TRUE)
defs <- get_infec_profile(hhdiscrete)
defs
```

It's important to keep in mind that by default we truncate the infectivity profile to avoid transmission to occur on day 0 of infection. 
The discrete profile is now a discretized gamma with the same parameters^[However, since the distribution is truncated the actual expected value will typically be different than the parameter `mean` in this case.]

```{r}
#| fig.alt: >
#|  Discrete instantaneous infectivity profile as a function of the generation day in black.
#|  On a second axis in orange, the corresponding cumulative infectivity profile.
profile <- expose_infec_profile(defs$func, defs$func_args, discr = TRUE)
infec <- dplyr::tibble(gentime = seq(0, 10, 0.01),
                       inst = profile$pdf(gentime),
                       cumul = profile$cdf(gentime))
rescale <- max(infec$cumul) / max(infec$inst)

ggplot(infec, aes(x = gentime)) +
  # plot cumulative profile
  theme(axis.ticks.y.right = element_line(color = "coral"),
        axis.text.y.right = element_text(color = "coral"),
        axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = "coral")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = cumul / rescale), color = "coral") +
  # plot instantaneous
  geom_line(aes(y = inst), color = "black") +
  # apply rescaling
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Daily",
                     sec.axis = sec_axis(~. * rescale, name = "Cumulative")) +
  labs(x = "Generation Day")
```

## Custom Infectivity Profiles

Imagine we would like to associate a gamma distribution as infectivity profile.
In this simple hypothesis all individuals will share the same profile which depends only on the generation time.
We can provide a custom infectivity profile calling `add_infec_profile()` as follows:

```{r}
hhdiscrete <- hhdiscrete |>
  add_infec_profile("gamma", shape = 4, scale = 1.3)
defs <- get_infec_profile(hhdiscrete)
defs
```

```{r}
#| fig.alt: >
#|  Custom discrete instantaneous infectivity profile in black.
#|  On a second axis in orange, the corresponding cumulative infectivity profile.
profile <- expose_infec_profile(defs$func, defs$func_args, 
                                min = defs$min, discr = TRUE)
infec <- dplyr::tibble(gentime = seq(0, 10, 0.01),
                       inst = profile$pdf(gentime),
                       cumul = profile$cdf(gentime))
rescale <- max(infec$cumul) / max(infec$inst)

ggplot(infec, aes(x = gentime)) +
  # plot cumulative profile
  theme(axis.ticks.y.right = element_line(color = "coral"),
        axis.text.y.right = element_text(color = "coral"),
        axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = "coral")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = cumul / rescale), color = "coral") +
  # plot instantaneous
  geom_line(aes(y = inst), color = "black") +
  # apply rescaling
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Daily",
                     sec.axis = sec_axis(~. * rescale, name = "Cumulative")) +
  labs(x = "Generation Day")
```

If the profiles, distributions or functions currently loaded in housepi are not sufficient to deal with your case study, we provided a mechanism to define custom functions.
Unfortunately, this requires some programming knowledge in C++.
We show how to deal with [User functions](user_functions.html) in the namesake vignette.
